title: At the hairdresser's
goal: Say what you had done with the causative: kestirdim, yıkattım, tamir ettirdim.

intro.text: The causative makes someone else do the action, and Turkish uses it for every service: *Saçımı kestirdim* (I had my hair cut), *Arabamı yıkattım* (I had my car washed). After a vowel in a longer stem it is *-t*; after most consonants, `-DIr`.

vocab.en: to sew; to put up (a stone, a building)
to make longer; to grow (your hair)

exercises.explain: *kes-* has one syllable and ends in a consonant, so the causative is `-DIr`, with t after s: *kes-tir*. Then the past *-di* and *-m*.

reject.why: *Yıkadım* is **I washed it** myself. For a service, add the causative *-t*: *yıka-t-tı-m*.
After a vowel in a longer stem, the causative is *-t*, not `-DIr`: *yıkattım*.

exercises.explain: *yıka-* ends in a vowel, so the causative is *-t*; after t, the past is *-tı*: *yıka-t-tı-m*.

exercises.question: Which sentence means **I had my hair cut**?

why.1: *Kestim* means you cut it yourself; the causative *-tir-* says someone else did.

exercises.explain: *kes-tir-di-m*: the hairdresser did the cutting, and you had it done.

exercises.label: *yaptırmak*, past: I had it done, you had it done…
exercises.explain: *yap-tır-* is a new stem, and the past endings follow as usual: *yap-tır-dı-m*.

exercises.prompt: We had the house painted last summer.

reject.why: *Boyadık* is **we painted it** ourselves. **Had it painted**: *boya-t-tı-k*.
The house is a definite object, so it takes the accusative: *evi*.

exercises.en: I'm going to have my computer repaired.

accept: I had this jacket made in Istanbul.
I had this jacket [sewn|tailored] in Istanbul.
I got this jacket [made|sewn|tailored] in Istanbul.
In Istanbul I had this jacket [made|sewn|tailored].

exercises.prompt: Where do you get your hair cut?

exercises.text: Saçımı ___, bu yüzden bu ay kestirmeyeceğim.
exercises.en: I'm growing my hair, so I won't get it cut this month.
exercises.explain: *uza-t-ıyor-um*: the causative of *uzamak* (to get longer), **I'm making it longer**. *Saçım uzuyor* would be **my hair is growing**.

exercises.en: Where did you have your car washed?

exercises.question: Which verb is the causative of *gelmek*, **to make (something) come**?

why.1: *Gelmek* is irregular: its causative is *getirmek*, **to bring**.
why.2: *-t* is only for longer stems ending in a vowel, l or r, and *gelmek* is irregular anyway: *getirmek*.

exercises.explain: Three common verbs have irregular causatives: *gör-* → *göster-* (show), *gel-* → *getir-* (bring), *kalk-* → *kaldır-* (lift).

exercises.prompt: Did you have your shoes repaired?

reject.why: *Tamir ettin* is **did you repair them** yourself. **Have them repaired**: *tamir ettirdin*.

accept: Will you show me your photos?
